methodological_questions: Does a one-for-one change in the offensive five shift the offense's shot-zone mix relative to a matched stint baseline?
Can the design distinguish a personnel effect from game-state, matchup, and shooter-selection confounding?
Is the design capable of returning a null, so that 'the design can detect personnel effects' is tested rather than assumed?
Are the lineup-change events and shot counts sufficient for useful power across 2022-23 to 2024-25?

historical_evidence.finding: Within-team-season on/off possession play-type shares: a shaper on the floor associated with CUT +1.353pp, PNR +0.98pp, SPOT_UP -1.248pp, DRIVE -0.542pp; 73 team-seasons (organizers 58). Recorded as supported, but it is a play-type mix result, not a shot-mix result, and its recorded risk is CONFOUNDING with no validation recorded.

Shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor: DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4), PPP +0.008 (t=+1.1) on N=1.07M possessions; recorded verdict WEAK/SMALL, will not carry a paper. Shows that an opponent-side personnel shift produced sub-1pp mix changes, and that the recorded limit was small sample.
Play-type mix after a key player's absence was described as nearly identical to the pre-absence mix (paper, no numeric table, no CI), n=148 spells.

No systematic volume pivot toward a better same-game option; 1,539 triggers analysed, recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Relevant as an example of a powered null in this project, not a lineup test.
Bonus-threshold and foul-trouble-big adaptation: the FTA jump (+5.08pp) is mechanical; DRIVE +0.31pp matched the 2-3 placebo +0.33pp; foul-trouble exposure only 1.44% of possessions.

PULL_UP exposure decline: -0.0255 with lineup FE fell to -0.0063 without lineup FE, and same-shooter placebo on other play types was -0.0075; recorded verdict artifact_found, attributed to shooter-level confounding.
On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from matchup/PBP fields: labelled 14.9% of DET possessions and 3.3% of ORL possessions; switches_on unpopulated; recorded as failed_gate.
Inferred defensive scheme change: 99.0% of units show change and transition matrices are near-uniform, which the record attributes to possible label noise.
Exposure slope for repeated play types: league-wide within-game -0.0019 (SE 0.0019); only PULL_UP survives Holm; team-trait split-half r +0.008, season-to-season +0.037 (low measurement reliability).

Team heterogeneity in halftime adaptation: heterogeneity variance not distinguishable from permutation null (p=0.363); split-half r -0.026; team-season slope SD 0.6733 vs mean sampling SE 0.6508 (low reliability).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling defensive coverage from matchup/PBP fields to use as a mechanism measure
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as failed_gate: only 14.9% and 3.3% of possessions labelled, switches_on field unpopulated, and label error and small sample flagged.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a shooter-level exposure decline to defensive adaptation without lineup controls
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact_found: the effect shrank from -0.0255 (lineup FE) to -0.0063 (no lineup FE), and the placebo on other play types was of similar size, indicating a shooter/lineup confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing offensive adaptation to a situational trigger (bonus, foul-trouble big) that is rare in the data
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: the main effect was mechanical (FTA jump) and the placebo matched the drive effect; exposure was sparse (1.44%).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a mix change after a personnel absence
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with no CI or numeric table, n=148; the mechanism is recorded as unclear (E_unclear).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting small shot-mix shifts from an opposing personnel change
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive/weak: sub-1pp shifts with PPP t=+1.1, SE of rim share 0.295, and the record notes small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game exposure-slope detection with noisy team-level measures
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits: insufficient exposure, label error, and low measurement reliability; only one play type survived Holm correction.

evidence_establishes: Project-level records show personnel-related shifts in play-type mix can be estimated within team-season on/off designs (FAM:SF-PAP-007, recorded as supported), so the general approach has precedent.
Personnel-side shot-mix shifts of the size seen in FAM:SF34 (sub-1pp, SE about 0.3pp at about 1.07M possessions) are small and were not established as significant at that sample.
Mechanism-driven and label-driven approaches in this project have repeatedly produced artifacts or unanswerable results (FAM:SF-CHT-076, FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
No retrieved record tests a one-for-one offensive-five change against shot-zone mix with a negative-control design.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a change of offensive five moves shot-zone mix (rim, mid, 3PA) in these seasons. No retrieved record reports this outcome for offensive-lineup change events.
Whether the design can detect a personnel effect. The question's own phrasing presupposes this; no record validates a detection benchmark.
Effect size, power, or the number of qualifying lineup-change events for 2022-23 to 2024-25.
Whether FAM:SF-PAP-007's play-type shift survives a shot-mix outcome or a lineup-level confounder adjustment (its recorded validation status is no_validation_recorded).
own_inferences: The question as posed is circular: 'showing the design can detect personnel effects' is written as the conclusion. A positive result is needed to validate the design, so the design needs a negative-control arm to make a null informative.
Coach substitutions respond to score, fouls, fatigue, and matchups, so lineup changes are not random; the lineup-change effect is confounded with game state unless matched on it.
Shot mix is not the same as play-type mix. FAM:SF-PAP-007 is evidence that personnel shifts appear in play-type mix, not evidence about shot zone.
Given the sub-1pp magnitudes in FAM:SF34, a single-season test may be underpowered; pooling 2022-23 to 2024-25 and using the playoffs as a holdout is more sensible.
Shot-zone outcomes derived from distance and result can be sensitive to clock and possession-end effects, which need to be controlled.
uncertainties: Number of one-for-one offensive-five change events in the data is unknown.
Whether the rotation-interval and starter fields reliably identify on-court five at each possession is not documented in the retrieved records.
The derived play-type records are built from PBP with possible outcome leakage into labels.
Whether a shot-zone classification from shot distance is reliable is not documented.
Whether NBA rule and pace changes across 2022-25 cause drift that confounds seasonal comparisons is unknown.
No retrieved record reports a validation status for shot-mix outcomes (most recorded as no_validation_recorded).

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that similar personnel and adaptation tests in this project returned artifacts (lineup-FE and mechanical-trigger artifacts), untestable labels, or sub-1pp inconclusive shifts. That moves the decision from a straight proceed to proceed with changes: the design must include matched game-state controls, a lineup-FE check, a placebo lineup-change arm, and a pre-specified power calculation before any positive claim is made.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup changes are selected by coaches on score, fouls, fatigue and matchup; without matched controls and a lineup-FE check, shot-mix differences cannot be attributed to personnel (FAM:SF-TMP-009 shows this pattern).
Recorded personnel shot-mix shifts are sub-1pp (FAM:SF34); the number of clean one-for-one change events per season is unknown and may not reach useful power.
Detection depends on a placebo arm (non-shot-relevant swaps or other play types) that must come out null for the result to be credible.

prior_work.summary: Related personnel and matchup questions were studied: on-floor shaper shifts in play mix (supported, confounded), opponent big-off-floor shot mix (sub-1pp, inconclusive), absence-based play-mix stability (inconclusive, no CI), and lineup-FE artifacts. None directly tests whether a one-for-one offensive-five change moves shot-zone mix with a negative control, so the question is only partly answered.

risks.text: Substitutions are endogenous to game state and matchups; need matched stints and lineup/matchup fixed effects (cf. FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-PAP-007).
Lineup changes chosen in response to foul trouble, score, or fatigue; selection on these must be modelled or matched.
Sub-1pp effects (FAM:SF34) need many clean change events; power not yet computed.
Specific one-for-one swaps of key players may be rare, leaving thin cells (cf. FAM:SF-CHT-076 at 1.44%).
Rotation-interval and starter fields may misattribute on-court five; reliability is undocumented (cf. FAM:SF38, FAM:SF-TMP-016).
Shot-zone and play-type labels may be noisy (cf. FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
Derived play-type possession records from PBP may encode the outcome, so mix shifts may be partly definitional.
Lineup or shot-mix features computed from the full game (including later substitutions or outcomes) would leak future information into the change indicator.
A positive result depends on a placebo arm being null; cf. FAM:SF-TMP-009 and FAM:SF-CHT-076 where placebos flagged artifacts.
Several shot zones, lineup types, and seasons create many comparisons; Holm correction needed (cf. FAM:SF38).
Rule, pace, and shot-profile trends across 2022-23 to 2024-25 may shift baselines; season fixed effects are needed.
Possession-to-lineup joins across substitutions and period boundaries are error-prone and need validation.

design.estimand: Within-stint change in offensive shot-zone share (rim, mid-range, 3PA) when one offensive player is replaced by another, relative to the pre-change baseline of the same team and game, conditional on game state and defensive matchups. The question is reframed as a test of whether the design detects personnel effects: detection is established only if the positive arm is significant and the negative-control arm is null.
design.unit: Offensive possession, with stint-level change indicators; shot-level outcomes aggregated to possession.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 for the discovery and confirmatory split (by season); playoffs held out as an out-of-sample check. Include only clean one-for-one swaps occurring at non-dead-ball times with starters and rotation intervals validated against PBP.
design.power: Not yet computed. Compute minimal detectable shot-share shift for the number of eligible swap events before running; pre-register a minimum of 80% power at alpha 0.05 for a 1pp shift (the FAM:SF34 scale). If power is inadequate, report as untestable rather than null.
design.controls: Team, opponent, and season fixed effects; game-state controls (score margin, period, clock, fouls, bonus status); defensive matchup fixed effects (opposing five or rim big on floor); shooter-level fixed effects; pre-change team tendencies (rolling 10-game baseline); lineup fixed effects as a robustness check (FAM:SF-TMP-009). Leakage guard: all covariates measured before the change.
design.falsification: Negative-control arm: one-for-one swaps of players with no shot-mix role (for example, a non-shooting or injury-return swap) and swaps that do not change the on-court five; both must show no shot-zone shift. Placebo outcome: free-throw share and turnover rate, which should not respond to personnel swaps by construction. The positive claim fails if the placebo arm shows a comparable shift.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across shot zones and lineup-type subgroups; a single pre-specified primary outcome (3PA share) and a single primary contrast.
design.decision_rule: Design is judged to detect personnel effects only if (a) the primary 3PA or rim-share contrast is significant after Holm and (b) the negative-control and placebo arms are null with CIs excluding the primary effect size. If the primary contrast is null and power is adequate, report a powered null. If power is inadequate or the placebo is non-null, report untestable or artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, box score, 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular and playoffs, with derived play-type records (Neo4j INITIATED edges) used only as a secondary check due to possible outcome-derived labels.

methodological_questions: Can changing the offensive five detect personnel effects on shot mix?
What confounders threaten attributing shot-mix change to lineup change rather than game context?
Is the substitution design powered and reliable for detecting shot-mix shifts across 2022-23 to 2024-25 seasons?
How do rotation intervals and partial possession matchup data affect measurement validity?
args.query: lineup change effect on shot mix offensive five substitution design NBA play-by-play personnel detection

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
